items.text: CUET (UG) 2026 is one entrance test whose scores are used for admission to undergraduate programmes at all Central Universities and other participating universities for the 2026-27 session.
items.note: Page numbers for this Information Bulletin are PDF page numbers; the printed page number is one less.

items.text: The test is conducted by the National Testing Agency (NTA), an autonomous body set up by the Ministry of Education under the Societies Registration Act, 1860.

Participating universities include Central, State, Deemed and Private universities; the test is meant to give students across the country, including rural and remote areas, a single window for applying.
NTA only registers candidates, conducts the test, publishes and finalises answer keys, declares results and hosts score cards. Merit lists and counselling are done by the universities.
Questions about admission, merit lists or counselling must go to the university concerned, not to NTA.
In 2026, 15,68,867 unique candidates registered and 11,64,098 appeared. The test ran over 19 days in 35 shifts.
The 2026 test was held in 321 exam cities, including cities outside India.
items.note: The result press release of 23 June 2026 says 13 cities outside India. The press release of 07 June 2026 (https://nta.ac.in/Download/Notice/Notice_20260608081249.pdf, page 1) says 15 international cities and also names Dubai and Munich.

items.text: There is no age limit for taking CUET (UG) 2026.
Candidates who have passed Class 12 or an equivalent exam, or who are appearing for it in 2026, can take the test.
Candidates must still meet any age rule of the university or institution where they want admission.

Accepted qualifying exams include: Class 12 from a recognised central or state board (such as CBSE or CISCE); two-year intermediate or pre-university; the NDA Joint Services Wing two-year course; NIOS senior secondary with at least five subjects; HSC vocational; a 3-year AICTE or state-board diploma; GCE A level; Cambridge HSC; and the IB Diploma.

Any other board or foreign exam must be recognised as equivalent to Class 12 by AIU, UGC or an agency notified by the Ministry of Education. Candidates from outside India or an unlisted board need a UGC equivalence certificate.
If Class 12 was not a public exam, the candidate must have passed at least one earlier public (board or pre-university) exam.
Each university sets its own rules on year of passing, minimum marks, subject combinations, quota and reservation. Check the university website before applying.
Taking CUET (UG) does not guarantee admission. The candidate must also meet the programme-wise eligibility of the university.
Candidates taking an improvement or re-appear exam in Class 12 should choose 'Passed' in the form.
Reserved seats for OBC-NCL, Gen-EWS, SC, ST and PwD/PwBD candidates follow Government of India or state rules. The benefit depends on document verification.
Eligible PwBD candidates can get a scribe and compensatory time of 20 minutes for each hour of the exam.
items.note: The scribe and compensatory time rules are on PDF pages 19-21.

items.text: Mode: Computer Based Test (CBT) only.
There are 37 subjects in total: 13 languages, 23 domain-specific subjects and 1 General Aptitude Test.

A candidate can choose up to 5 subjects, counting languages and the General Aptitude Test. The choice does not have to match Class 12 subjects; it should match what the chosen university and programme require.
Each test paper has 50 objective multiple-choice questions, and all of them are compulsory.
Each test paper lasts 60 minutes.
Marking: +5 for a correct answer, -1 for a wrong answer, 0 for an unanswered question.
If more than one option is found correct, +5 goes to anyone who marked any of the correct options. If no option is correct, or a question is wrong or dropped, every candidate who appeared gets +5.
Question papers are available in 13 languages: English, Hindi, Assamese, Bengali, Gujarati, Kannada, Malayalam, Marathi, Odia, Punjabi, Tamil, Telugu and Urdu.
The paper is shown in English and in the medium the candidate chose. The medium cannot be changed after applying. If the two versions differ, the English version counts.
A candidate can take Hindi as the language test and English as the medium for the other tests, as long as this suits the university's requirements.
The exam runs in multiple shifts. In 2026 each shift lasted 3 hours, and a candidate could be given 1 to 3 subjects in one shift. A candidate with 2 subjects in a shift could leave after 2 hours.
items.note: The Information Bulletin (PDF page 16) says only that the exam is held in multiple shifts.

items.text: Questions in all testing areas are set at the level of the NCERT syllabus.
Languages (codes 101-113): English, Hindi, Assamese, Bengali, Gujarati, Kannada, Malayalam, Marathi, Odia, Punjabi, Tamil, Telugu, Urdu.

Domain subjects (23): 301 Accountancy/Book Keeping, 302 Agriculture, 303 Anthropology, 304 Biology/Biological Science/Biotechnology/Biochemistry, 305 Business Studies, 306 Chemistry, 307 Environmental Science, 308 Computer Science/Information Practices, 309 Economics/Business Economics, 312 Fine Arts/Visual Arts/Commercial Arts, 313 Geography/Geology, 314 History, 315 Home Science, 316 Knowledge Tradition - Practices in India, 318 Mass Media/Mass Communication, 319 Mathematics/Applied Mathematics, 320 Performing Arts (Dance, Drama, Music), 321 Physical Education (Yoga, Sports), 322 Physics, 323 Political Science, 324 Psychology, 325 Sanskrit, 326 Sociology.
General Aptitude Test: code 501.
Language tests check reading comprehension (factual, literary and narrative passages), literary aptitude and vocabulary.
Domain subject tests follow the NCERT syllabus.

The General Aptitude Test covers general knowledge, current affairs, general mental ability, numerical ability, basic quantitative reasoning (arithmetic, algebra, geometry, mensuration, statistics), and logical and analytical reasoning.
Sanskrit (325) is a domain subject and is not translated into other languages. Students of traditional Shastric subjects applying to the three central Sanskrit universities may choose Sanskrit (325).
The official subject-wise syllabus PDFs for 2026 are listed on the CUET (UG) 2026 syllabus page.
Applications are made online only, at https://cuet.nta.nic.in. Each candidate may submit only one form; more than one form leads to cancellation of the result.
Step 1, registration: fill in basic details, set a password and a security question, and note the Application Number the system generates.
Step 2, application form: log in and fill personal and education details, choose universities and programmes, test papers and exam cities, and upload images and documents.

Photographs: capture a live photo by webcam (or by scanning a QR code with a phone) and upload a recent colour passport photo. The photo must show 80% of the face, ears visible, no mask, on a white background, as a 10-200 KB JPG/JPEG.
Signature: 10-50 KB JPG/JPEG. Disability/UDID certificate: 50-300 KB PDF. Identity proof, only if not verifying through Aadhaar or DigiLocker: 10-200 KB JPG/JPEG.
Step 3, fee payment: pay online by net banking, credit card, debit card or UPI. Bank processing charges and GST are extra.
Step 4, confirmation page: it appears only after the fee is paid successfully. Download and keep it. The application counts as complete only once the fee is received.
If the confirmation page does not appear after payment, contact the bank or payment gateway. If needed, pay again; any duplicate payment is refunded after NTA reconciles fees.
Fees once paid are not refunded.
Choose up to four exam cities, only within the state of the permanent or present address. NTA may allot a different city.
Use one mobile number and one email per form. They may belong to a parent or guardian.
Documents from DigiLocker are accepted. An APAAR ID is not required. A name mismatch between the Class 10 marksheet and Aadhaar does not affect candidature.
items.note: The DigiLocker answer (FAQ 6) is on page 1.

items.text: Only some fields can be changed, and only during the correction window NTA announces. NTA does not accept corrections by post, fax, WhatsApp, email or by hand.
The 2026 correction window was a one-time chance. Changes that raised the fee needed extra payment, and excess payments were not refunded.
Password rules: 8-13 characters, with at least one upper-case letter, one lower-case letter, one number and one special character.
Everything is done online. Do not send any document, including the confirmation page, to NTA by post or any other way.
General (UR): ₹1000 for up to 3 subjects, plus ₹400 for each extra subject.
OBC-NCL / Gen-EWS: ₹900 for up to 3 subjects, plus ₹375 for each extra subject.
SC / ST / PwD / PwBD / Third gender: ₹800 for up to 3 subjects, plus ₹350 for each extra subject.
Exam centres outside India: ₹4500 for up to 3 subjects, plus ₹1800 for each extra subject.
Bank processing charges and GST are paid on top of the exam fee. Bank-wise charges are listed in Appendix IV of the Information Bulletin.
Only OBC candidates in the central OBC-NCL list may choose OBC. State-list OBC candidates who are not in the central list must choose General.
Fees can be paid through SBI, Canara Bank, ICICI Bank or HDFC Bank by debit card, credit card, net banking, UPI or wallet.
2026 cycle, as first announced: online application 03-30 January 2026 (up to 11:50 PM); fee payment by 31 January 2026; correction 02-04 February 2026.
items.note: The same dates are in the Information Bulletin, PDF page 7. They were later extended (see the next item).

items.text: 2026 cycle, extended: application to 04 February 2026; fee payment to 07 February 2026; correction window 09-11 February 2026 (up to 11:50 PM).
items.note: The 09 February 2026 notice confirms the 09-11 February correction window.

items.text: 2026 cycle: the application and fee portal re-opened from 23 February 2026 (afternoon) to 26 February 2026 (11:50 PM). No corrections were allowed after submission in this window.
2026 cycle: candidates who had paid could update their chosen subjects from 17 to 19 April 2026 (up to 11:50 PM).
2026 cycle: advance exam city intimation slips were released on 29 April 2026.
2026 cycle: admit cards could be downloaded from 05 May 2026.
2026 cycle: the exam was announced for 11-31 May 2026 (tentative).
2026 cycle: exams set for 28 May 2026 (both shifts) were postponed because the Id-ul-Zuha (Bakrid) holiday date changed.
2026 cycle: the exam was actually held on 11-31 May 2026 and 06-07 June 2026.
items.note: The 06-07 June dates were for rescheduled candidates (notices of 30 May and 01 June 2026).

items.text: 2026 cycle: provisional answer keys could be challenged from 09 to 11 June 2026 (up to 10:00 PM); the fee had to be paid by 11 June 2026 (11:50 PM).
2026 cycle: results (NTA scores) were declared on 23 June 2026.
NTA's revised exam calendar (December 2026 to April 2027) does not list CUET (UG) 2027. No 2027 dates have been announced.
items.note: Revised calendar notice dated 26 October 2026: https://nta.ac.in/Download/Notice/Notice_20261026114247.pdf

sections.title: City intimation slip and admit card

items.text: NTA first releases an advance city intimation slip, which shows the exam city and the subject-wise schedule. Log in to download it. It is not the admit card.
The admit card is issued provisionally on https://cuet.nta.nic.in. It is not sent by post, and the candidate must download it.
Receiving an admit card does not mean the university has accepted the candidate's eligibility; that is checked later during admission.
Candidates must take the exam at the centre, date and shift on the admit card. Requests to change the date or shift are not accepted.
If you cannot download the admit card, or its details are wrong, call 011-40759000 (10 AM - 5 PM). If details are wrong, take the exam with the downloaded card and NTA will correct its records later.
No duplicate admit card is issued at the exam centre. Altering an admit card is treated as unfair means.
In 2026, 79% of candidates got their first-choice city and 96.6% got one of their chosen cities. A re-allocation window was opened for the rest.
items.note: Press release dated 05 May 2026.

items.text: In 2026, candidates whose live photo did not match Aadhaar, or who registered with another ID, had to bring a certificate attested by their principal/headmaster or a Class-I gazetted officer, in the format from NTA's 07 April 2026 notice.
Reach the exam centre 2 hours before the exam starts.
No one is let in after the gate closes. Forcing entry or arguing with staff is treated as unfair means.

Must carry: a printed admit card with the self-declaration (A4); one passport photo (same as uploaded); a simple transparent ball-point pen; and one original, valid photo ID (school ID, PAN, passport, Aadhaar or e-Aadhaar with photo, Class 12 board admit card with photo, or bank passbook with photo).
PwD/PwBD candidates claiming relaxation must bring their certificate. Diabetic candidates may carry sugar tablets or fruit.

Not allowed: printed or written material, geometry or pencil boxes, calculators, pens, scales, erasers, pen drives, log tables; mobile phones, Bluetooth devices, earphones, health bands; wallets, goggles, handbags, belts, caps; watches, bracelets, cameras; ornaments or metal items; food and water bottles.
items.note: For 2026, NTA's advisory of 07 May 2026 (https://nta.ac.in/Download/Notice/Notice_20260507204424.pdf) said all candidates could carry transparent water bottles.

items.text: Bulletin dress code: heavy clothes with long sleeves and shoes are not allowed; slippers and low-heeled sandals are allowed.
items.note: Differs from the 07 May 2026 advisory (https://nta.ac.in/Download/Notice/Notice_20260507204424.pdf). The advisory said light clothing is preferred, woollens are allowed if candidates report early for frisking, and normal shoes, slippers and low heels are the preferred footwear.

items.text: Candidates wearing articles of faith (for example a religious thread such as kalava) should report well before the last reporting time so they can be frisked.
items.note: The bulletin (PDF page 30) asks such candidates to report at least two hours before the last reporting time.

items.text: All candidates are frisked with metal detectors before entry. Female candidates are frisked by female staff in a closed enclosure.
Sit only at the seat allotted to your roll number, and check that the paper on screen is the subject on your admit card.
Do all rough work on the rough sheets provided. Write your name and application number on each sheet and hand them to the invigilator at the end.
There is no re-test for candidates who miss their scheduled exam for any reason.
NTA posts the provisional answer keys on https://cuet.nta.nic.in with a public notice, usually for two to three days.
Recorded responses and attempted question papers are shown before the result. Download your response sheet, because it is not provided later.
Challenging an answer costs ₹200 per question. The fee is paid online and is not refunded.
items.note: The same fee appears in the Information Bulletin, PDF page 31.

items.text: Only paid challenges made through the official link within the time window are considered. Supporting documents go in a single PDF; challenges without justification are not considered.
Steps: open 'Challenge(s) regarding Answer Key', log in with Application Number and password, view the question paper, tick the option IDs you claim, upload your proof, submit, then pay.
Subject experts review all challenges. Candidates are not told individually whether their challenge was accepted. Results are prepared from the final answer key.
The final answer keys for CUET (UG) 2026 were published by NTA.
items.note: The CUET (UG) site also links a copy: https://cdnbbsr.s3waas.gov.in/s3d1a21da7bca4abff8b0b61b87597de73/uploads/2026/06/202606231857909583.pdf

items.text: CUET (UG) 2026 results (NTA scores) were declared on 23 June 2026.
Score cards are not posted. Download them from the CUET (UG) website by logging in.
items.note: Information Bulletin, PDF page 32.

items.text: For subjects held in more than one shift, raw marks are converted to NTA scores. Marks are normalised separately for each subject using the equi-percentile method.
items.note: The summary is on PDF page 32; the full method is in Appendix VI, PDF pages 59-68.

items.text: There is no re-evaluation or re-checking of results.
The CUET (UG) 2026 score is valid only for admissions in academic year 2026-27.
After results, each university announces its own counselling and admission schedule and merit list. NTA has no role in preparing merit lists.
A complaint about the result is considered only if raised within 30 days of the result. Disputes fall under Delhi/New Delhi jurisdiction.
In 2026, 332 unique question papers (18,160 questions) were set, and 996 papers were administered across all 13 languages.
The official list is on the CUET (UG) site in five groups: Central, State, Deemed and Private Universities, and Other Government Institutions.
244 universities took part in CUET (UG) 2026, up from 241 in 2025.
items.note: When fetched on 2026-11-12, the website lists also added up to 244 entries: 49 Central, 41 State, 27 Deemed, 120 Private and 7 Other Government Institutions.

items.text: The Information Bulletin lists 48 Central Universities, based on course mapping as of 03 January 2026.
items.note: The later website list of Central Universities (https://cuet.nta.nic.in/participating-universities/central-universities/) has 49 entries. It adds IIT Dharwad and shows HNB Garhwal University under a shorter name.

items.text: The list of participating universities changes over time. Programme details and eligibility are on each university's own website. The website list also links a PDF for each university.
CUET (UG) help desk: email cuet-ug@nta.ac.in; phone 011-40759000 or 011-69227700.
items.note: The same contacts are in the Information Bulletin, PDF page 13.

items.text: NTA general help desk: genadmin@nta.ac.in; phone 011-40759000 or 011-69227700.
Admit card helpline hours: 10:00 AM to 5:00 PM on 011-40759000.
Official websites: https://cuet.nta.nic.in and https://nta.ac.in.
Legal notices and petitions can be served on NTA only at legal@nta.ac.in.
NTA's address on notices from September/October 2026 is 5th Floor, Government of India Press Building, Minto Road, New Delhi - 110002.

unknown: No CUET (UG) 2027 Information Bulletin, application dates, exam dates or fees have been published as of 2026-11-12. NTA's revised calendar (26 Oct 2026, up to April 2027) does not list CUET (UG) 2027.
We cannot tell whether the 2027 pattern (37 subjects, up to 5 subjects, 50 questions, 60 minutes, +5/-1) or the fees will change.
Shift timings for 2026 were not given in the bulletin ('to be informed later') and appeared only on admit cards. They are not recorded here.

We captured only the titles of these notices, not their contents: 04 Dec 2025, 27 Dec 2025, 27 Jan 2026, 07 Apr, 14 Apr, 30 Apr, 05-06 May (city/date/shift facility), 10 May, 27 May, 30 May and 01 Jun 2026. Most are scanned images.
Dates of notices we did not open come from the timestamp in NTA's file name. For the final answer key notice (2026-06-21), the printed date was not confirmed.
The official list of participating universities does not give each university's state, so the state column in universities-CUET_UG.csv is empty.
The 'Contact Us' link on cuet.nta.nic.in returned a 404 error on 2026-11-12, so only the NTA Help Desk page was used for contacts.
The unfair-means chapter of the bulletin (PDF pages 28-29) and the full scribe procedure are not summarised here.
